# Verification analysis: outbound-nat-mapping-rhel9

Job: `2026-09-05__12-23-47`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` routes between `lan-a` and `lan-b`. When `node2` on `lan-a` opens a
> connection to `node3` on `lan-b`, have `node3` observe it as arriving from
> an address of your choosing on `node1` rather than from `node2`'s own
> address, while connections in the other direction keep their original
> source.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 opnsense + 2 rhel9.8**
- Networks: **mgmt, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node2**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `outbound-nat-mapping-rhel9__CwbTLsr`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently satisfied: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b, node2->node3 traffic is verified by live tcpdump capture to arrive at node3 sourced from node1's chosen address (192.168.20.1) rather than node2's real address, and node3->node2 traffic is verified to retain node3's original source address, with a pre/post-NAT control confirming causation. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was executed on all three nodes with pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and a full end-to-end re-verification of the asymmetric NAT behavior after all restarts. Hygiene is good, with only minor unremoved diagnostic log residue in /tmp on each node.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.940 | 52/5 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **routing — Satisfied:** node1 routes between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3)
  - **Why:** opt1 (192.168.10.1) and opt2 (192.168.20.1) interfaces were configured and reconfigured on node1; node2 and node3 both successfully ping their respective gateway and ping across the router to each other (cmd-5a3c1cba84b54400, cmd-eae8b60f252d4bc0, cmd-31915d9b9b5043ce), directly demonstrating routing between the two segments.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-aefde441124f4a18`, `cmd-5a3c1cba84b54400`, `cmd-eae8b60f252d4bc0`, `cmd-31915d9b9b5043ce`
- **snat-forward — Satisfied:** node2->node3 (lan-a to lan-b) traffic appears at node3 as originating from a chosen address on node1, not node2's own address
  - **Why:** An outbound NAT rule (source 192.168.10.0/24 out opt2 -> 192.168.20.1) was added and loaded into pf (cmd-c8a48c38c8254d8a, cmd-0020e237620f498a). tcpdump on node1's lan-b-facing interface during a node2->node3 ping directly shows the packet as '192.168.20.1 > 192.168.20.2' (cmd-0278ec104f324a1c), i.e. sourced from the chosen node1 address rather than node2's 192.168.10.2. A before/after control (cmd-18c0901a7c12482c/cmd-3ae7f6d9534a4586 pre-NAT showing 192.168.10.2 as source vs cmd-0278ec104f324a1c post-NAT) isolates the NAT rule as the cause.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c8a48c38c8254d8a`, `cmd-0020e237620f498a`, `cmd-188fc03f0fc34626`, `cmd-3c70b3266b424f48`, `cmd-0278ec104f324a1c`, `cmd-18c0901a7c12482c`, `cmd-3ae7f6d9534a4586`
- **no-nat-reverse — Satisfied:** node3->node2 (lan-b to lan-a) traffic keeps its original source address
  - **Why:** tcpdump on node1's lan-a-facing interface during a node3->node2 ping shows the packet as '192.168.20.2 > 192.168.10.2' (cmd-040f3120a40f4f91), i.e. node3's real address is preserved, confirming the NAT rule is directional and does not affect the reverse flow.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1a44bf85d1824989`, `cmd-ab5c11bc0254480d`, `cmd-040f3120a40f4f91`
- **restart-protocol — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with recovered state
  - **Why:** For each node the trace shows a pre-restart boot identity/health baseline (cmd-7989b6cd98944d7c, cmd-d581473847fd467d, cmd-2e9ac788d8784f60), a restart acknowledgement plus a period of unreachability (cmd-2009083df24b4dd8/cmd-db4c12ed0fef4b77, cmd-78cfa233ac784afd/cmd-7572644f7ed24e0a, cmd-63a1021bb5f64314/cmd-1ad4bf0b99334ab4), a differing post-restart boot identity confirmed against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service/data state including re-verified IP/route config, connectivity pings, persisted NAT/interface configuration, plus a full end-to-end re-run of the asymmetric NAT tcpdump test after all three restarts (cmd-5f3ef84357a74d64 through cmd-e17c4c2153784e31).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7989b6cd98944d7c`, `cmd-2009083df24b4dd8`, `cmd-db4c12ed0fef4b77`, `cmd-3c2caa1b2c134e24`, `cmd-88f9fb518a884ef5`, `cmd-d581473847fd467d`, `cmd-78cfa233ac784afd`, `cmd-7572644f7ed24e0a`, `cmd-324705d8f5ec448c`, `cmd-0741e06ed8344e81`, `cmd-2e9ac788d8784f60`, `cmd-63a1021bb5f64314`, `cmd-1ad4bf0b99334ab4`, `cmd-0ee55d9ac95945cb`, `cmd-ec91923bafca4494`, `cmd-5f3ef84357a74d64`, `cmd-81d730e6d1af4151`, `cmd-dde85e9728744585`, `cmd-e4399c6e8ba14401`, `cmd-e17c4c2153784e31`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`

### Comments and limitations

- Only ICMP (ping) traffic was used to demonstrate the NAT and routing behavior; the task did not specify a protocol/port and ICMP-based SNAT verification is a reasonable proxy for 'opens a connection', but TCP/UDP connection-level behavior was not separately exercised.
- Minor diagnostic log residue (tcpdump captures, reboot.log) was left in /tmp on all three nodes and not cleaned up, though this does not affect functional correctness.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.900); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.940; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
